question: Explain Porter's five forces model for analysing the competitive environment of an industry.

points.label: Threat of new entrants
points.description: New firms add capacity and compete for share; the threat is lower when entry barriers such as scale, capital needs and brand loyalty are high.
points.basis: Porter's five forces: threat of new entrants

points.label: Bargaining power of buyers
points.description: Strong buyers can push prices down or demand better quality, especially when they buy in bulk or can switch easily.
points.basis: Porter's five forces: bargaining power of buyers

points.label: Bargaining power of suppliers
points.description: Strong suppliers can raise prices or reduce quality, especially when there are few of them or no close substitutes for their inputs.
points.basis: Porter's five forces: bargaining power of suppliers

points.label: Threat of substitutes
points.description: Products from other industries that meet the same need limit the price an industry can charge.
points.basis: Porter's five forces: threat of substitute products

points.label: Rivalry among existing firms
points.description: Competition through price, advertising and new products is intense when there are many similar competitors, slow growth or high exit barriers.
points.basis: Porter's five forces: rivalry among existing competitors

points.label: Use of the model
points.description: Together the forces decide the profit potential of an industry and help a firm find where it can position itself.
points.basis: Porter's five forces: purpose of industry analysis
